purpose: Complete original open problems, statement formalization only

entries.scope: Sharp universal asymptotic l(N) ~ sqrt(N) for arbitrary finite real sets; both bounds encoded.
entries.status_note: Underlying problem attributed to Riddell 1969; sharp conjecture verified directly on Erdős 1973 p.120. May 2026 lower constant remains below 1.

entries.name: Riddell–Erdős progression-free subset ratio
entries.date_note: Riddell introduced the extremal functions in 1969. The all-k ratio question is explicit in Erdős 1975, pp. 306–307.
entries.scope: For every fixed k >= 3, R_k(N)/G_k(N) tends to 1, where R_k is the maximum progression-free subset size in [1,N] and G_k is the minimum such maximum across all N-element integer sets.
entries.status_note: The problem page highlights k=3. The formalization retains the entire original progression-length family. Constant-factor comparison is partial.
entries.duplicate_status: no match found in checked catalog/upstream
entries.claim_screen: No full-resolution claim found in the 2026-10-22 bounded screen.

entries.name: Erdős linear minimum degree in 4-critical graphs
entries.date_note: Conservative upper bound on proposal date: in the 1993 source Erdős says he asked this more than 20 years earlier; exact first year not identified.
entries.scope: There is epsilon > 0 and arbitrarily large n with an n-vertex edge-critical four-chromatic simple graph of minimum degree at least epsilon*n.
entries.status_note: Formalizes the positive answer to the original question. The 2026 linear upper bound with coefficient 3/10 is partial, not a resolution.
entries.duplicate_status: no match found in checked catalog/upstream
entries.claim_screen: No full-resolution claim found in the 2026-10-22 bounded screen.

entries.name: Erdős–Purdy degenerate quadruples
entries.scope: For every epsilon > 0, all sufficiently large finite planar sets A have at most |A|^(3+epsilon) four-point subsets with fewer than six distinct pair distances.
entries.status_note: Original question on printed p.251. Equal-distance pairs may share an endpoint; restricting to four distinct endpoints would weaken it.
entries.duplicate_status: no match found in checked catalog/upstream
entries.claim_screen: No full-resolution claim found in the 2026-10-22 bounded screen.

entries.name: Marcus–de Oliveira determinantal conjecture
entries.scope: For all complex normal matrices A,B of every positive order, det(A+B) lies in the real convex hull of products of pairwise sums over all permutations of their complete eigenvalue lists.
entries.status_note: The 2026 paper proposes a stronger conjecture, not a proof. Structured matrix and small-order results do not settle arbitrary normal pairs.
entries.duplicate_status: no match found in checked catalog/upstream
entries.claim_screen: No full-resolution claim found in the 2026-10-22 bounded screen.

entries.name: Minkowski inhomogeneous product conjecture
entries.date_note: Conservative documented-by date; the conjecture is older.
entries.scope: Every nonsingular real n-by-n matrix A and real shift b admit an integer z with product_i |(Az-b)_i| <= |det A|/2^n, in every positive dimension.
entries.status_note: Known low-dimensional results do not resolve all dimensions. Distinct from Brunn–Minkowski and Minkowski lattice-tiling conjectures.
entries.duplicate_status: no match found in checked catalog/upstream
entries.claim_screen: No full-resolution claim found in the 2026-10-22 bounded screen.

entries.name: Cantoni's three-Hamilton-cycle conjecture
entries.scope: Every planar cubic finite simple graph with exactly three undirected Hamilton cycles contains a triangle.
entries.status_note: All graph orders retained. Verification through order 48 and later restrictions are partial.
entries.duplicate_status: no match found in checked catalog/upstream

entries.name: Marcus block-permanent conjecture
entries.scope: For every complex Hermitian PSD block matrix A, permanent(A) >= permanent([permanent(A_ij)]); with block size >= 2 and positive definite diagonal blocks, equality iff every off-diagonal block is zero.
entries.status_note: Both the inequality and its original equality clause are retained. Two-block and low-rank results are partial. Different from the Marcus–Minc transform conjecture, now claimed proved.
entries.duplicate_status: no match found in checked catalog/upstream
entries.claim_screen: No full-resolution claim found in the 2026-10-22 bounded screen.

entries.name: Wang's Hadamard permanent question
entries.scope: Every real sign Hadamard matrix of order > 2 has nonzero permanent; encoded over integers, without a Sylvester or circulant restriction.
entries.status_note: Formalizes the negative answer to the original zero-permanent existence question. Finite-order checks and the all-order Sylvester result are partial. Other solved Wang questions about resemblance classes or maximum permanents are different.
entries.duplicate_status: no match found in checked catalog/upstream
entries.claim_screen: No full-resolution claim found in the 2026-10-22 bounded screen.

selection_rule: Discard any identified full proof or disproof claim for the exact problem, even if unaccepted. Partial results do not by themselves trigger exclusion.
